questions.prompt: What is a fungus most closely described as?
options: A living organism of its own kingdom, neither plant nor animal
A type of plant that photosynthesizes
questions.explanation: Fungi form their own kingdom of living things - mushrooms, molds, and yeast - which are neither plants nor animals.
questions.misconception: Because a mushroom looks like a plant, many think fungi are plants. But they belong to their own kingdom and do not photosynthesize.

questions.prompt: What is the main body of most fungi?
options: A network of fine threads (hyphae) called mycelium, mostly underground
The round cap of the mushroom
questions.explanation: The hidden network of threads called mycelium is the main body; what you see above ground is usually just the fruiting body releasing spores.
questions.misconception: People often think the mushroom cap is the whole fungus. In fact the cap is only the spore-producing fruiting body and the spread mycelium threads below are the main body.

questions.prompt: How do most fungi get their food?
options: By releasing enzymes that break apart material and absorbing the nutrients
questions.explanation: Fungi are decomposers - they release enzymes to break down dead material and then absorb the dissolved nutrients.
questions.misconception: Unlike plants, fungi do not make food from sunlight; they break down existing material and absorb the nutrients.

questions.prompt: How do fungi reproduce and spread?
options: By releasing tiny spores that grow into new fungi
By growing big seeds like plants
By dividing only with a host cell
questions.explanation: Fungi make tiny spores, often from the mushroom cap, which spread and grow into new fungi where they settle.
questions.misconception: Fungi relate raise no seeds and need no host. They use tiny spores spread to reproduce, quite unlike viruses.
